## This package implements the University of Cincinnati color scheme for Quarto revealjs presentations

All color names used follow those from the color palette defined at <https://www.uc.edu/about/marketing-communications/brand-guide/visual-identity/color.html>

Background gradients are defined here:
<https://www.uc.edu/about/marketing-communications/brand-guide/visual-identity/gradients-textures.html>

## The "official UC red gradient" background {.official-uc-red-gradient}

The official UC red gradient background can be added to a slide in Quarto through the `official-uc-red-gradient` class:

```{markdown}
## This will give your slide an official UC red gradient background {.official-uc-red-gradient}
```

## The "beyond black gradient" background gradient slide {.beyond-black-gradient}

UC's secondary gradient, called "beyond black", can be added to a slide in Quarto through the `beyond-black-gradient` class:

```{markdown}
## This will give your slide a beyond black gradient background {.beyond-black-gradient}
```

## The UC "white gradient" background {.white-gradient}

UC's other secondary gradient, called "white", can be added to a slide in Quarto through the `white-gradient` class:

```{markdown}
## This will give your slide a white gradient background {.white-gradient}
```

## A flat UC red background {.uc-red-flat}

A flat UC red background can be added to a slide in Quarto through the `uc-red-flat` class:

```{markdown}
## This will give your slide a flat UC red background {.uc-red-flat}
```

## A flat UC black background {.uc-black-flat}

A flat black background can be added to a slide in Quarto through the `uc-black-flat` class:

```{markdown}
## This will give your slide a flat black background {.beyond-black-gradient}
```

## A black and white slide {.black-and-white}

Without applying any of the custom classes to the slides, the `ucinci` style package will give you slides with a white background, black text, and red secondary elements. If you need a slide that has no red elements, you can invoke the `black-and-white` class.

```{markdown}
## This will give your slide black text, black navigation, and a white background {.black-and-white}
```

## You can provide your own background image on the title slide

To use your own background on the title slide, the `title-slide-background` can be defined in your Quarto document's YAML header. The file location should be relative to your main document. Included within the resources folder is the picture of Baldwin Hall used in the College of Engineering and Applied Science official PowerPoint template as a webp file:

`title-slide-background: "_extensions/ucinci/images/baldwin.webp"`

## Title slide background image modifications

The additional available parameters (and defaults) are:   
`title-slide-background-size: cover`       
`title-slide-background-position: center`         
`title-slide-background-repeat: no-repeat`        
`title-slide-background-opacity: 1`  

## Title slide text and navigation colors

The text and navigation colors on the title slide can be controlled through the `title-slide-classes` property in the YAML header. The available classes to use are those background options described in previous slides:
`title-slide-classes: [official-uc-red-gradient]`

Additional custom classes could be added by modifying `ucinci.scss`.

When using a background image with transparency, you can control the background color within the UC color schema with these same classes. For example,
`title-slide-background: "_extensions/ucinci/images/baldwin.webp"`
`title-slide-classes: [beyond-black-gradient]`
will render Baldwin Hall with a black background instead of UC red.

## Title slide logo

The package places a UC logo on each page except for the title page. A logo can be placed on the title slide using the YAML parameter `title-slide-logo`. This enables different logos to be used depending on the title slide appearance, and enables different unit lockups to be used.
`title-slide-logo: "_extensions/ucinci/images/my_unit_lockup.png"`

The resources folder contains a logo for UC and lockups for the College of Engineering and Applied Science and the Department of Mechanical and Materials Engineering.
`title-slide-logo: "_extensions/ucinci/images/UC_MME_STACKED-04-05.png"`

## Title slide extensions beyond standard Quarto

* The ucinci `title-slide` partial renders an ORCID symbol and link next to the authors' names when provided in the document yaml.
* An additional metadata parameter, `jobtitle`, can be supplied under author. This will render the job title between the author's name and affiliation, following the CEAS PowerPoint template.
* All UC brand colors are defined as css root variables. For example, they can be called up to be applied to a text span in Quarto using  `[This text should be white with a black background]{style="color: var(--white); background-color: var(--uc-black);"}`. The following options exist:
    - UC primary colors: [uc-red]{style="color: var(--uc-red)"}, [uc-black]{style="color: var(--uc-black)"}, [uc-white]{style="color:var(--white); background-color:var(--uc-black);"}
    - UC secondary colors: [uc-dark-red]{style="color: var(--uc-dark-red)"}, [grey]{style="color: var(--grey); background-color: var(--uc-black)"}
    - UC extended palette: [calhoun-maroon]{style="color: var(--calhoun-maroon)"}, [steger-silver]{style="color: var(--steger-silver)"}, [main-street-mist]{style="color: var(--main-street-mist)"}, [bearcats-black]{style="color: var(--bearcats-black)"}, [gettler-gold]{style="color: var(--gettler-gold)"}, [tangeman-tan]{style="color: var(--tangeman-tan)"}

::: {.fragment}
The color names are identical to those defined in the UC color palette. I don't know why the decision was made to call regular black `UC black` but regular white is not `UC white`. I don't know why `grey` is spelled according to the UK dictionary either, since [the US had an English language spelling reform in 1828.](https://www.merriam-webster.com/about-us/spelling-reform#:~:text=Noah%20Webster%20was%20struck%20by,filled%20only%20with%20British%20textbooks.)
:::

## Add a source citation to the bottom of the slide

When you have a source that you want to cite on a slide, you can add the `.source-citation` class to a div to place it in the bottom left of the slide. For example, `[This is a source citation]{.source-citation}`

or

```{markdown}
::: {.source-citation}
This is a source citation.
:::
```

will place "This is a source citation" in tiny gray font at the bottom of the slide. This way we can give credit where credit is due without distracting from the main content of the slide. The styling of this element can be modified by changing the `.source-citation` class in `revealjs-supplement.css`.

For example: people learn more from words and pictures together than from words alone (the *multimedia principle*). The source for that claim is at the bottom left of this slide.

::: {.source-citation}
R. E. Mayer, *Multimedia Learning*, 2nd ed. Cambridge, U.K.: Cambridge University Press, 2009.
:::

## Make figure captions not extend beyond the width of the image

In the reveal css, the figure captions are allowed to go the full width of the slide. This can result in them being offset from their images.

We add a class `.caption-match-image` that can fix this.

In can be invoked in two ways. The first is to add the class to the image element itself:

```{markdown}
![Caption](image.png){.caption-match-image}
```

The second is to wrap the image in a div with the class:

```{markdown}
::: {.caption-match-image}
![Caption](image.png)
:::
```

# Other official UC slide background images

The background images in this section come from the CEAS PowerPoint template, enabling the user to recreate this template in Revealjs presentations. They are provided in the resources folder.

## Logo-shadow {.uc-red-flat background-image="_extensions/ucinci/images/logo-shadow.jpg"}

The `_extensions/ucinci/images/logo-shadow.jpg` background works well with the `.uc-red.flat` or `.official-uc-red-gradient` classes. To use `logo-shadow.jpg` as a background, apply the background-image attribute with a class that changes the text color from the default like this:
```{markdown}
## Logo-shadow {.uc-red-flat background-image="_extensions/ucinci/images/logo-shadow.jpg"}
```

## Baldwin-Alt {.uc-red-flat background-image="_extensions/ucinci/images/baldwin-alt.jpg"}

The `_extensions/ucinci/images/baldwin-alt.jpg` background is included for completeness. This is part of the CEAS powerpoint template and differs from the other picture of Baldwin Hall through transparency in the bottom left triangular region.

Use of this background is not recommended at this time because it differs in color display from `baldwin.webp`, the image used for the title slide. In the case of `baldwin.webp`, I have modified it such that the image is formed by an alpha layer overlaid on the correct UC red web color, `#E00122`. If you really want to use the original PowerPoint background image rather than the one with improved colors, you can find it in the resources folder as `baldwin-orig.jpg`.

## Electronics {.uc-red-flat background-image="_extensions/ucinci/images/electronics.jpg"}

The electronics background image is `_extensions/ucinci/images/electronics.jpg`. It is included for completeness only. Despite being part of the CEAS powerpoint template, it differs from the UC official web colors in a way that seems more apparent in revealjs than in PowerPoint, similar to `baldwin-alt.jpg`.

## Diagonals {.black-and-white background-image="_extensions/ucinci/images/diagonals.jpg"}

The `_extensions/ucinci/images/diagonal.jpg` background is included for completeness, but is not recommended at this time as this package is currently written to make logos, navigation elements, page numbers, and the footer to render as the same color. If you really wanted to use this background, probably the `.black-and-white` class is your only option. However, this would not meet the [UC color combination guidelines](https://www.uc.edu/about/marketing-communications/brand-guide/visual-identity/color.html). It is not possible to meet the style guidelines with the *current* background classes in `ucinci.scss`. I might try to add independent control of the colors of navigation elements, logo, footer, and page numbering in a future release to better work with different background images.

## Element-header {.black-and-white background-image="_extensions/ucinci/images/element-header.jpg"}

The `_extensions/ucinci/images/element-header.jpg` background is included for completeness, but is not recommended as the text placement in revealjs will not reliably fall on top of the title as the page is resized.

## Plain-header {.black-and-white background-image="_extensions/ucinci/images/plain-header.jpg"}

The `_extensions/ucinci/images/plain-header.jpg` background is also included for completeness, but is not recommended as the text placement in revealjs will not reliably fall on top of the title as the page is resized.

# Content classes

## The bang box

Use `.bang-box` for the one sentence on a slide that students must not miss. It is UC red with white bold text, centered, and stays red on `.white-gradient` and `.black-and-white` slides.

```{markdown}
::: {.bang-box}
Equilibrium is the minimum of the Gibbs energy, not of the enthalpy.
:::
```

::: {.bang-box}
Equilibrium is the minimum of the Gibbs energy, not of the enthalpy.
:::

## Two- and three-column grids {.nonincremental}

`.two-col` and `.three-col` lay out their children in equal columns (CSS grid), a lighter-weight alternative to Quarto's `::: {.columns}`.

```{markdown}
::: {.three-col}
**Heat** flows from hot to cold.

**Work** moves a boundary.

**Mass** carries energy across.
:::
```

::: {.three-col}
**Heat** flows from hot to cold.

**Work** moves a boundary.

**Mass** carries energy across.
:::

## Colored labels, centered text, and framed diagrams {.nonincremental}

::: {.two-col}
::: {}
- [`.label-teal`]{.label-teal}, [`.label-amber`]{.label-amber}, and [`.label-red`]{.label-red} color-code terms, e.g. [reactants]{.label-teal} → [products]{.label-red}.
- `.center-text` centers a block; `.center-column-text` centers the text in a column.
- `{.diagram}` on an image gives it a thin rounded frame and fills its column.

```{markdown}
[products]{.label-red}
![](figure.png){.diagram}
```
:::

::: {.center-text}
![](_extensions/ucinci/images/electronics.jpg){.diagram fig-alt="The CEAS electronics background image, shown here in a framed diagram style."}

This caption is centered with `.center-text`.
:::
:::

## Font sizes, logos, and incremental lists {.hide-logo .nonincremental}

- `## Slide title {.hide-logo}` hides the UC logo on that slide (as on this one), for a full-bleed figure.
- Lists appear one item at a time by default. `## Slide title {.nonincremental}` shows every list on that slide at once (as here). A `::: {.nonincremental}` div does the same for one list.
- `.font-tiny` … `.font-HUGE` set a LaTeX-style size on any span or div (see the font size slide).

```{markdown}
## A figure that needs the whole slide {.hide-logo .nonincremental}
```

# Learning objectives

## The objectives box

`.objectives-box` frames a numbered list of objectives. `.bloom-R`, `.bloom-U`, `.bloom-Ap`, `.bloom-An`, `.bloom-E`, and `.bloom-C` tag the Bloom's level; `.learning-objective-number` and `.module-M1` … `.module-M5` add badges. PDF and beamer output get the same look from `objectives-style-tex.lua`.

```{markdown}
::: {.objectives-box}
By the end of this session, you will be able to:

1. Calculate $\Delta G^\circ$ for a reaction from tabulated data. [Ap]{.bloom-Ap} · [#36]{.learning-objective-number}
2. Describe what an Ellingham diagram represents. [U]{.bloom-U} · [#75]{.learning-objective-number} [M5]{.module-M5}
:::
```

::: {.objectives-box}
By the end of this session, you will be able to:

1. Calculate $\Delta G^\circ$ for a reaction from tabulated data. [Ap]{.bloom-Ap} · [#36]{.learning-objective-number}
2. Describe what an Ellingham diagram represents. [U]{.bloom-U} · [#75]{.learning-objective-number} [M5]{.module-M5}
:::

## A long objectives box that scrolls

Add `.scroll-box` to any box that may run off the slide: `::: {.objectives-box .scroll-box}`. Each click reveals the next objective and scrolls it into view; stepping back scrolls back.

::: {.objectives-box .scroll-box}
By the end of this session, you will be able to:

1. Remember the definitions of a system, its surroundings, and its boundary, and classify a system as open, closed, or isolated. [R]{.bloom-R} · [#1]{.learning-objective-number}
2. Explain the difference between a state function and a path function, giving two examples of each from everyday experience. [U]{.bloom-U} · [#2]{.learning-objective-number}
3. Apply the first law to calculate the heat and work for a reversible isothermal expansion of an ideal gas. [Ap]{.bloom-Ap} · [#3]{.learning-objective-number}
4. Analyze a heat-capacity measurement to separate the electronic and lattice contributions at low temperature. [An]{.bloom-An} · [#4]{.learning-objective-number}
5. Evaluate whether a proposed process violates the second law, using the entropy change of the universe. [E]{.bloom-E} · [#5]{.learning-objective-number}
6. Create a Gibbs energy–composition diagram for a regular solution and use it to construct a miscibility gap. [C]{.bloom-C} · [#6]{.learning-objective-number}
7. Apply the Gibbs–Helmholtz relation to find how an equilibrium constant changes with temperature. [Ap]{.bloom-Ap} · [#7]{.learning-objective-number}
8. Analyze an Ellingham diagram to predict which of two metals reduces the other's oxide at a given temperature. [An]{.bloom-An} · [#8]{.learning-objective-number}
:::

## A scroll box for any content {.nonincremental}

`.scroll-box` works on any div. When there is nothing inside to reveal, each click scrolls the box down by most of its height.

::: {.scroll-box style="border: 2px solid var(--steger-silver); border-radius: 8px; padding: 0 0.6em;"}
{{< lipsum 1-4 >}}
:::

# Fragments

## Collapsing fragments for a sliding derivation {.nonincremental}

reveal.js's `.fade-out` leaves an invisible, same-size gap. Add `.collapse-out` so the step also gives up its space, and the steps below slide up smoothly.

```{markdown}
::: {.fragment .fade-out .collapse-out data-fragment-index="1"}
$G = H - TS$
:::
```

::: {.fragment .fade-out .collapse-out data-fragment-index="1"}
**Step 1:** $G = H - TS$
:::

::: {.fragment .fade-out .collapse-out data-fragment-index="2"}
**Step 2:** $dG = dH - T\,dS - S\,dT$
:::

**Step 3:** $dG = V\,dP - S\,dT$ (this step stays)

::: {.fragment data-fragment-index="2"}
**Step 4:** at constant $T$ and $P$, $dG = 0$ at equilibrium
:::

# Math and notes

## Chemistry with `\ce{}` {.nonincremental}

Math is rendered with KaTeX. Chemical formulas and reactions can be written with mhchem's `\ce{}` inside math; the format loads KaTeX's mhchem extension only when a document uses it (and the `mhchem` LaTeX package for PDF output).

```{markdown}
$\ce{2Fe + O2 -> 2FeO}$, $\ce{Fe2O3(s) + 3CO(g) -> 2Fe(l) + 3CO2(g)}$,
$\ce{H2O <=> H+ + OH-}$, $\ce{^{235}_{92}U}$
```

$\ce{2Fe + O2 -> 2FeO}$, $\quad\ce{Fe2O3(s) + 3CO(g) -> 2Fe(l) + 3CO2(g)}$

$\ce{H2O <=> H+ + OH-}$, $\quad\ce{^{235}_{92}U}$

## Speaker notes and instructor notes {.smaller}

- `::: {.notes}` are reveal.js speaker notes: press **S** to open the speaker view. They also print in PDF and handout output.
- `::: {.instructor-notes}` never reach the slides, not even the speaker notes (anyone with a copy of the HTML can press S). They appear only in a PDF whose format sets `instructor-notes: true`, as a boxed "Instructor notes" callout.

```{markdown}
::: {.notes}
Ask who has seen a blast furnace. (Everyone can see this.)
:::

::: {.instructor-notes}
The answer key is on the back of the handout. (Instructor printout only.)
:::
```

```yaml
format:
  ucinci-revealjs: default
  pdf:
    instructor-notes: true      # the instructor printout
filters:                        # needed for formats other than ucinci-revealjs
  - _extensions/paytonej/ucinci/resources/scripts/instructor-notes.lua
```

::: {.notes}
This slide's speaker note: everyone with the HTML can read it.
:::

::: {.instructor-notes}
You will not find this text anywhere in the rendered slides.
:::

## PDF, handout, and Canvas helpers {.smaller}

The extension also ships filters and post-render scripts for the other outputs of a course project. Add them under `filters:` or `post-render:` in `_quarto.yml`:

| File (in `resources/scripts/`) | What it does |
|---|---|
| `objectives-style-tex.lua` | Objectives box and badges in PDF and beamer |
| `pdf-image-width.lua` | `{width="850px" pdf-width="60%"}`: a separate image size for PDF |
| `latex-image-alt.lua` | Passes `fig-alt` into tagged PDFs for accessibility |
| `fix_pdf_fonts.py` | Repairs LuaLaTeX font subsets that Acrobat rejects |
| `compress_pdf.py` | Compresses rendered PDFs |
| `quarto_html_to_canvas_fragment.py` | Turns HTML output into a Canvas page body |
| `sync_to_onedrive.py` | Copies rendered files to the folder named in `_secrets.json` |

The PDF title partial also accepts `date-string: "Fall 2026"` to print literal text instead of a parsed date.

## Live polls {.smaller .nonincremental}

:::: {.two-col}
::: {}
Students vote on their phones; the slide shows a countdown, then the results. Mark correct answers with `[x]`.

````markdown
::: {.poll time=45 position="bottom-left"}
Which particle melts at the lower temperature?

- [x] The 5 nm particle
- [ ] The 50 nm particle
:::
````

In PDFs, handouts, and HTML pages the same block becomes a lettered question with no answer marked.
:::

::: {}
Polls need the small PHP server in [`poll-server/`](https://github.com/paytonej/ucinci-revealjs/tree/main/poll-server), plus:

```yaml
revealjs-plugins: [poll]
filters:
  - _extensions/paytonej/ucinci/resources/scripts/poll.lua
poll-server: https://your.server.edu/~you/poll
```

The secret key goes in `_secrets.json` (`"poll_key"`), which stays out of git. Rendering writes it into decks that contain a poll, and nowhere else.
:::
::::

# Classroom activities

## Activity partials {.smaller .nonincremental}

Drop-in slide pieces for class activities, added with Quarto's `include` shortcode. After `quarto add`, they are in `_extensions/paytonej/ucinci/resources/partials/`:

| Partial | What it does | Data |
|---|---|---|
| `countdown.qmd` | Click-to-start timer in the slide's top-right corner | Minutes from `{data-countdown="12"}` on the slide (default 15) |
| `think-pair-share.qmd` | Think (1:15) → pair (1:45) → share timer, then draws three names | Roster |
| `team-draw-2.qmd` … `team-draw-6.qmd` | A full slide that deals the roster into 2–6 random teams | Roster |
| `three-week-calendar.qmd` | Due dates, class days, and breaks for three weeks | Schedule workbook |

- **Roster:** `Roster.xlsx` (or a `.csv`) with a `First Name` column, or set `roster_file = "..."` in an earlier code cell. With no roster, sample names are used, as in this demo. Keep the real roster out of public repositories.
- **Schedule:** `schedule.xlsx`, or set `cal3_workbook`. The comments at the top of the partial describe its three sheets ([an example](https://github.com/paytonej/ucinci-revealjs/blob/main/demo-schedule.xlsx)).
- These partials run Python, so the document needs `jupyter: python3` and pandas/openpyxl.

## Code annotation

```{.python code-line-numbers="1-7|1|3|4|1-7"}
import numpy as np # <1>

def f(x): # <2>
    return np.sin(x) # <3>

# Example of a simple function using NumPy
f(0)
```

1. Importing the NumPy library.
2. Defining a function `f` that takes an argument `x`.
3. Returning the sine of `x` using NumPy's `sin` function.
